status: AI-generated concepts of the proposed installation.

design.stage: An orchestra-pit arrangement with curved rows of miniature chairs, music stands, cetacean figures and guide-instrument props. More than six permanent places; up to six selected per composition.
design.instruments: Bowed strings, flute, wooden mallets/marimba, reeds/clarinet, horn, tuba, organ and bells reflect the current guide sounds.
design.leds: Illuminated seat rings mark selection, brightness follows playing activity, and colour indicates conservation status.
design.sound: Room loudspeakers; a PC combines and generates audio and controls playback.
design.display: Separate synchronized audio visualizations with spectrograms and a playback playhead.
design.controls: Physical wired recording-site buttons on table/wall maps, or a touchscreen map blackboard. The floor-map variant uses a nearby accessible touchscreen.

prompts:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: landscape 3:2 architectural exhibition concept image for the Whale and Dolphin Orchestra Installation page.
Primary request: Correct this existing installation image to reflect the intended build. Preserve the warm museum/gallery, timber materials, daylight, human-scale proportions, camera angle, visitors and wheelchair accessibility. Treat the supplied image as the edit target, not an invitation to design a different room.
Orchestra: one continuous low timber orchestra stage containing TWELVE permanent cetacean positions, clearly more than six. Arrange twelve small whale and dolphin sculptures on twelve fixed circular seat bases, in three gentle curved rows of four. Anatomically distinct silhouettes include long-flipper humpback, large slender blue whale, blunt-headed sperm whale, tall-dorsal orca, right whale, fin whale, minke whale, beluga, pilot whale, bottlenose dolphin, common dolphin and spinner dolphin. Keep the figures stationary and physically fabricated; visitors do not carry, swap or move them. Keep all twelve visible and reasonably small. Remove extra miniature brass instrument props to make the species and LEDs clear.
Selection and playing: exactly SIX of the twelve circular seat bases have illuminated LED rings, while the other six bases are unlit plain timber. The lit six are spread across the stage, not a separate six-place stage. Selected rings have visibly different brightness, representing playing activity, with some bright and some softly glowing. Ring hue represents conservation status, not instrument or species identity: a right whale position glows red, a blue whale position orange, a fin whale position yellow, and humpback and dolphin positions green; the sixth selected position may be another green cetacean. Use restrained local LED light, not futuristic halos or whole glowing sculptures. All the remaining figures and bases are unlit but clearly present.
Sound and display: retain proper physical room loudspeakers on stands, with visible drivers. Remove ALL headphones, headphone hooks and headphone listening stations. Keep one real large wall display showing three clean synchronized horizontal audio strips, with labels exactly "RECORDED", "MEASURED", "GENERATED": spectrogram frequency textures and a measured pitch/onset trace sharing a single thin white vertical playback playhead. This is an audio analysis/playback display, not the selection interface. No aquarium films, decorative animal video, piles of interface panels, paragraphs or slogan text. A modest PC sits discreetly on the console below the display with neatly routed cables to speakers and controls; it handles combination, music generation and playback.
Style: photorealistic architectural concept render, believable matte printed or screen map, timber grain, fabricated animal sculptures, clear readable scientific sound display, natural soft daylight. No watermark, logo, projector, live animals, fantasy technology or added signs. This is an illustrative unbuilt installation proposal.

Specific edit for this version: retain the upright wood-framed touchscreen blackboard displaying a geographically recognizable entire world map. The visitor's fingertip selects a small recording-site dot directly on that touchscreen. Keep this map screen clearly distinct from the large spectrogram playback screen on the rear wall. Replace the six oversized animals on the foreground rounded stage with the twelve smaller fixed species figures and only six illuminated LED seat bases described above. Retain the warm wood finishes, woman's pose and natural daylight. Remove the bottom touchscreen cards showing animal photography; make the map a calm, almost full-surface interface with unobtrusive recording-site dots and a slim selection row, without readable new text. The map is on the touchscreen, not projected. No physical buttons on this touchscreen version.

Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: final correction to the interactive touchscreen concept.
Input images: Image 1 is the edit target. Image 2 is a supporting reference ONLY for the content of its rear wall audio visualization screen.
Primary request: Change ONLY the graphics inside the rectangular rear wall sound display of Image 1. Its current three waveforms should instead show real scientific audio visualization, like the screen in Image 2.
At the top, beside the exact label "RECORDED", show a time-versus-frequency SPECTROGRAM HEATMAP with many fine stacked frequency rows, teal-blue frequency texture and yellow curved harmonic call tracks; do not draw an amplitude waveform in this strip. In the middle, beside exact label "MEASURED", show sparse gold pitch contour curves and separate short gold onset ticks on a charcoal background. At the bottom, beside exact label "GENERATED", show an orange-red spectrogram heatmap of generated audio, with dense horizontal frequency bands and fine vertical note attacks. Use a single thin white vertical playback playhead through all three strips. No extra labels, borders, headings or menus.
Invariants: keep the entire rest of Image 1 unchanged: upright wood-framed world-map touchscreen and woman's touch gesture, the larger permanent whale/dolphin orchestra, exact figure positions and selected/unselected LED rings, PC below screen, proper loudspeakers, room, natural daylight, timber, camera and composition. Do not move or add any figures, change lights, add headphones or change any controls. Preserve original landscape 3:2 size and photorealistic style. No watermark.

Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: revised landscape 3:2 architectural installation concept.
Input image: Image 1 is the edit target. Preserve the exact gallery, people, visitor positions, map controls, loudspeakers, PC, wall audio visualization, daylight and framing.
Primary request: Redesign ONLY the whale-and-dolphin orchestra area into a clearly theatrical miniature ORCHESTRA PIT, with visible musical instruments. The current rounded wooden podium looks like a display cabinet; replace it with an orchestra-pit composition that has curved rows of small orchestra chairs and black music stands on a low dark stage. Preserve the rest of the image.
Orchestra-pit style: a broad shallow semicircular or horseshoe-shaped low stage with a charcoal-black interior floor, subtle curved timber rim, and three gently curved rows facing a small open conductor area. It should visually read as a traditional orchestra section, with distinct chairs, music stands, and instruments; not a stacked wooden exhibition plinth. The whole installation remains a freestanding human-scale gallery set-piece without digging into the gallery floor. Keep the front rim low and unobtrusive, no high barrier, no cage, and clear accessible paths around it.
Players: TWELVE permanent miniature cetacean positions, more than the six that can be selected for one piece. Twelve fabricated whale/dolphin figures, twelve miniature chairs and twelve slim black music stands, separated so the instrument silhouettes are visible. The animal figures are artistic sculptures perched or resting at their places beside their instruments; do not give whales human arms, clothes or fantasy limbs. Include a humpback, blue whale, right whale, fin whale, sperm whale, orca and several distinct dolphins and smaller whales. The figures stay fixed in the orchestra.
Musical instruments: bring back the instrument props. Clearly visible miniature cello/bowed-string instrument at the humpback place, silver flute for a dolphin, small wood marimba with mallets for sperm whale, clarinet/reed instrument for orca, French horn for right whale, tuba for fin whale, small organ pipes/keyboard for blue whale, bells or a small vibraphone for minke, and pan flute or ocarina at additional dolphin places. Use restrained realistic instrument miniatures with understandable shapes, not abstract clusters of brass sticks. Music stands and chair backs should establish an unmistakable orchestra-pit look. The props represent the guide instruments whose audio is made by the PC.
LEDs: keep small circular LED seat-position rings integrated unobtrusively into the floor at the bases of the chairs. Exactly SIX selected positions are lit at varied brightness, and the other six positions are completely unlit. Right-whale seat red, blue-whale seat orange, fin-whale seat yellow, humpback and two dolphin seats green. These colours indicate conservation status and brightness indicates playing activity. No glowing animal bodies or lights on every player.
Invariants: preserve the physical or touchscreen map input already shown, preserve the screen's labels "RECORDED", "MEASURED", "GENERATED" and one playback playhead, proper speakers, lack of headphones, PC, visitors including wheelchair user where present, timber gallery and natural daylight. No extra people, no moved map, no changed controls, no projector, no logos, no watermarks. Photorealistic exhibition concept; animal figures, chairs, music stands and instruments are all miniatures, not real animals or human-size whales.

Version-specific invariants: Keep the woman selecting a site on the upright world-map touchscreen blackboard and the separate spectrogram screen behind the stage.
